content.overview: Commissioning demonstrates that a newly installed or materially changed system performs as intended under defined conditions. A commissioning plan should identify system boundaries, sensors, controlled outputs, alarms/interlocks, test states, acceptance criteria and the evidence required before operational release.

vocabulary.definition: Structured verification that a system is installed, configured and performing as intended before routine operational reliance.
The documented pre-test or accepted reference state used for later comparison.
A predefined requirement that must be satisfied before the tested function is accepted.

sections.title: Commission functions, not labels
sections.body: Verify that the identified sensor, controller output and physical equipment response correspond to the intended zone/function rather than assuming labels or dashboard names are correct.

sections.title: Test the full command-response chain
sections.body: Exercise representative commands and verify equipment state plus measured crop-zone or irrigation response. A software indication alone is insufficient.

sections.title: Record acceptance and exceptions
sections.body: Preserve test method, result, deviation, temporary control and approval state so unresolved commissioning issues cannot disappear into routine operation.

workedExamples: A controller output labeled 'Zone 4 irrigation' activates a different valve during commissioning; the mismatch must be corrected and re-tested before acceptance.
commonMistakes: Accepting a system because every device powers on.
Fixing a labeling/configuration issue without preserving the failed commissioning evidence.
content.practicalApplication: Create a commissioning matrix for one environmental and one irrigation control loop with command, expected equipment response, representative measurement, alarm/interlock check and acceptance criterion.
content.summary: Commissioning turns design intent into verified operational evidence.
